items.description: The Sirte Basin is a major sedimentary basin in Libya, containing the country's largest oil reserves.
Jebel Aswad is a prominent volcanic relief feature in the southern Libyan desert, characterized by its dark color.
The relief of Wadi Mathendous consists of deep sandstone canyons that have preserved ancient engravings for millennia.
Wadi al-Farigh is a significant dry valley and depression located in the Cyrenaica region of eastern Libya.
The relief of Sarir Tanezrouft is remarkably flat and featureless, forming a vast expanse of gravel desert.
Gaberoun Lake is a deep saltwater lake set within the towering sand dunes of the Ubari Sand Sea.
The Mandara Lakes are a group of oasis lakes located in the deep valleys of the Fezzan sand dunes.
The Kufra Basin is a large structural depression in southeastern Libya, containing a vast underground aquifer.
The relief of the Gargaf Desert is dominated by high, stony plateaus and steep escarpments.
The Cyrenaica Coast relief features steep cliffs and narrow coastal plains overlooking the Mediterranean Sea.
